question: What is the typical length range of a normal adult fallopian tube?
explanation: Standard adult fallopian tubes typically measure between 10 and 12 centimeters in length, though individual variations do occur. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h1)

question: In which part of the fallopian tube does fertilization of the ovum normally take place?
explanation: The wider ampulla section provides the ideal space and environment for the sperm to meet and fertilize the released egg. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h1)

question: How can an unusually long fallopian tube affect the movement of an egg?

options.A: It slows down movement and can trap the egg inside
options.B: It stops the uterus from making female hormones
options.C: It completely stops the ovary from releasing eggs
options.D: It speeds up movement so much that the egg is destroyed

explanation: When a tube is extra long or twisted, the muscle movements are less efficient, making it easy for the slow-moving egg to get stuck. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h2)

question: What are the two main mechanisms that move an egg through the fallopian tube?
explanation: Hair-like cilia on the lining cells and wave-like muscle contractions work together to push the egg along. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h2)

question: A patient with long fallopian tubes presents with sharp pelvic pain and spotting early in pregnancy. What is the main condition to suspect?
explanation: When an egg takes too long to travel, it can implant inside the tube instead of the uterus. This is called an ectopic pregnancy and needs quick medical attention. You are learning fast! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h3)

question: Why can a very long fallopian tube lead to difficulty getting pregnant?

options.A: The fertilized egg may not reach the uterus in time
options.B: The ovaries stop making eggs from stretching
options.C: The cervix closes up to block sperm

explanation: If the journey takes too long, the embryo might implant in the wrong spot or stop growing before it reaches the uterus. Every question makes you a better nurse! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h3)

question: Which diagnostic procedure uses a contrast dye and X-rays to outline the inside of the fallopian tubes?
explanation: An HSG involves passing dye through the cervix to visualize the shape and length of the fallopian tubes on X-ray. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h4)

question: Why do doctors often use laparoscopy to look closely at the fallopian tubes?

options.A: It requires no anesthesia and is done at the bedside
options.B: It completely cures all tubal blockages
options.C: It uses high-frequency sound waves to measure organ density
options.D: It lets the surgeon see the pelvic organs directly with a camera

explanation: A laparoscope is a tiny lighted camera that gives the surgeon a clear, direct view of what is going on inside the pelvis. You're mastering this topic! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h4)

question: What is a key nursing priority when taking a health history from a patient with possible tubal problems?

options.A: Checking daily blood pressure and cholesterol
options.C: Testing the patient for gestational diabetes
options.D: Asking about past ectopic pregnancies and pelvic infections

explanation: Past infections and previous ectopic pregnancies give us vital clues about scar tissue or changes in the tubes. Keep up the great study habit! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h5)

question: Which symptom should immediately alert a nurse to a possible ectopic pregnancy?

options.B: Itching and thick white vaginal discharge
options.C: One-sided lower belly pain and abnormal spotting
options.D: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles

explanation: Pelvic pain on just one side, combined with light bleeding during early pregnancy, is a classic warning sign we always watch out for. Excellent! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h5)

question: What is the surgical term for the complete removal of a fallopian tube?
explanation: Salpingectomy is the surgical removal of one or both fallopian tubes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h6)

question: What is an essential nursing check after a patient has surgery on their fallopian tubes?

options.A: Measuring hand grip strength in both arms
options.B: Checking for active bowel sounds in the chest
options.C: Monitoring vital signs closely for internal bleeding
options.D: Testing the patient's eyesight every hour

explanation: Any surgery near pelvic blood vessels carries a risk of bleeding, so keeping a close eye on vital signs helps catch complications early. Proud of your daily progress! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T25#GNS216_U5_T25_h6)
